definitions.gloss: national polity; national structure; form of government
definitions.explanation: The fundamental character or political structure of a nation. Historically significant in prewar Japan as an ideological concept centering on the emperor system.
Short for 国民体育大会 (National Sports Festival), an annual multi-sport competition held in a different prefecture each year. Renamed to 国民スポーツ大会 in 2024, but the abbreviation 国体 remains in common use.

examples.japanese: {国体|こくたい}の{護持|ごじ}を{主張|しゅちょう}する。
examples.english: To advocate for preserving the national polity.

examples.japanese: {戦前|せんぜん}は{国体|こくたい}という{概念|がいねん}が{政治|せいじ}の{中心|ちゅうしん}にあった。
examples.english: Before the war, the concept of national polity was at the center of politics.

examples.japanese: {国体|こくたい}に{出場|しゅつじょう}する。
examples.english: To compete in the National Sports Festival.

examples.japanese: {来年|らいねん}の{国体|こくたい}は{地元|じもと}の{県|けん}で{開催|かいさい}される。
examples.english: Next year's National Sports Festival will be held in our home prefecture.

examples.japanese: {高校|こうこう}{時代|じだい}に{国体|こくたい}の{代表|だいひょう}{選手|せんしゅ}に{選|えら}ばれた。
examples.english: In high school, I was selected as a representative athlete for the National Sports Festival.

examples.japanese: {終戦|しゅうせん}{時|じ}、{政府|せいふ}は{国体|こくたい}の{維持|いじ}を{最優先|さいゆうせん}{条件|じょうけん}とした。
examples.english: At the end of the war, the government made preserving the national polity its top priority condition.

notes: This word has two very different meanings depending on context. Sense 1 ({国体|こくたい} = national polity) is a historically loaded term, central to prewar Japanese ideology emphasizing the emperor as the foundation of the state. It appears frequently in discussions of Japanese wartime history. Sense 2 is an abbreviation of {国民|こくみん}{体育|たいいく}{大会|たいかい}, Japan's annual national athletic competition held since 1946. Context usually makes the intended meaning clear: political/historical contexts point to sense 1, sports contexts to sense 2.
